title: How bacteria are engineered to make human insulin
examples: How is insulin made by bacteria?

explain.say: Millions of people with diabetes need insulin every day. It used to come from the pancreas of pigs and cows. Today, much of it is made by bacteria carrying a human gene! Let's see how scientists do it.

explain.say: Look at the first box. Scientists find the gene for insulin, a short stretch of human DNA. Then they use restriction enzymes, which are like molecular scissors, to cut it out. What tool would you use to cut paper?

explain.say: Now the puzzle piece. Bacteria have small rings of DNA called plasmids. Scientists cut a plasmid open with the same scissors and glue the insulin gene in with an enzyme called ligase. Why use the same scissors on both?

explain.say: See the germ? The new plasmid is put into bacteria. The bacteria read the human gene and start making human insulin. Then they are grown in huge steel tanks called fermenters. How fast do you think bacteria multiply?

faq.a: A gene is a section of DNA that holds the instructions to make one protein, such as insulin.
asks: Tell me about the insulin gene

faq.a: Restriction enzymes cut DNA at particular base sequences, often leaving short single-stranded ends called sticky ends that can pair up with matching ends.
asks: Tell me about cutting the gene out

faq.a: A plasmid is a small ring of DNA found in bacteria, separate from their main chromosome. Scientists use plasmids as vectors to carry new genes into bacteria.
A fermenter is a large steel tank where conditions such as temperature, pH, food and oxygen are carefully controlled so microorganisms grow fast and make lots of product.

faq.q: Why is bacterial insulin better than animal insulin?
faq.a: It is identical to human insulin, so it causes fewer allergic reactions, and it can be made in large amounts without relying on animals.

facts: Human insulin made by genetically modified bacteria was approved for medical use in 1982.
Restriction enzymes cut DNA, and DNA ligase joins pieces of DNA together.
